heard: Jupiter's famous storm plunges 200 miles deep into its atmosphere. Most people assume it's just a thin surface cloud. NASA's Juno spacecraft measured the planet's gravity to look inside. It revealed a vertical vortex reaching far below the cloud tops. These storm routes stretch past where solar light can reach. Since Jupiter lacks a solid surface, there's no friction to stop it. That lack of surface friction is why the storm plunges 200 miles deep.
